sourceEvidence.label: Local Guard and reporting source evidence

assessment.summary: The source supports a reproducible local preview with consent and fail-closed release disclosures, plus two structural production gates: an owned desktop channel and authenticated quarantined reporting.

nonNegotiables: No automatic reporting or Site Tool invocation.
Synthetic and local exercises never enter external intake or a feed.
One-use authority is consumed before awaited work and never retried automatically.
Every automated result and report carries the required self-reported-evidence limitation.
assumptions: No signing identity, production identity provider, moderation operator, approved retention policy, or performance budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Own the Local Guard authority boundary
opportunities.summary: Separate a reproducible developer preview from a signed desktop product with an OS-owned browser-to-host channel.
opportunities.diagnosis: The enforcement code is narrow, but unpacked installation and loopback HTTP leave publisher and inter-process authority at a development boundary.

evidence.claim: The extension requests activeTab, scripting, storage, and exact loopback hosts only.
The service worker owns document binding, permit validation, consume-before-execute, and no-retry enforcement.
A general desktop release needs publisher identity and a stronger local channel; packaging alone cannot remove compromised-host risk.
The source-ready browser client exposes a closed, bounded, request-correlated native-message action set with no retry.
The source-ready protocol binds one exact extension origin and rejects cross-origin pair requests, hidden fields, malformed frames, and oversized messages.
The non-mutating Windows plan binds one signed executable and exact store extension ID to an HKCU native-host manifest.

desiredInvariants: Every shipped byte is allowlisted and integrity-recorded.
A general release has a verifiable publisher and update identity.
The browser-to-host channel accepts only the installed extension identity.
Document-bound one-use authority cannot survive navigation, expiry, mismatch, or disconnect.

options.title: Reproducible loopback preview
options.summary: Keep exact loopback transport and add a deterministic allowlisted ZIP, hashes, and an explicit preview release channel.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Packaging fails when MV3 permission or host authority differs from the reviewed allowlist.
Existing document and one-use enforcement remains the runtime control.
Release integrity improves, while trusted-local-machine and unpacked-identity risks remain explicit.

tradeoffs.assessment: The artifact rejects reviewed permission, file, symlink, popup-reference, and dynamic-code drift; runtime transport is unchanged.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Reproduce ZIP bytes and inspect members, permissions, hosts, and hashes on two clean checkouts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Packaging does not change the runtime path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare connector startup and invocation latency with the unpacked baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: No process or retained runtime object is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm idle RSS remains within baseline variance.

tradeoffs.assessment: A fixed artifact reduces missing-file and unreviewed-file release mistakes; connector failures are unchanged.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Install the generated artifact in a fresh profile and repeat all five lessons.

tradeoffs.assessment: Release review must retain ZIP and hash metadata, but no new service exists.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run one release rehearsal and record operator time and failure points.

tradeoffs.assessment: The same runtime files are packaged; unpacked loading remains available.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm existing pairing and lesson tests against packaged and unpacked copies.

residualRisks: The extension is unsigned and the loopback/browser-profile trust boundary remains.
A reproducible artifact is not publisher identity or store review.

workPackages: Create deterministic artifact and integrity manifest.
acceptanceCriteria: All five lessons pass without retries.
migrationNotes: Label the artifact developer preview and retain unpacked fallback.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Withdraw the preview ZIP, revoke sessions, and return testers to the reviewed unpacked directory.

options.title: Signed native-host product
options.summary: Use a signed extension and installer with extension-ID-bound native messaging and stdio or OS-owned IPC.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A signed identity strengthens but does not replace exact manifest authority.
The native channel narrows transport exposure while service-worker policy remains required.
It narrows local channel and publisher risk but cannot defend a compromised OS/profile.

tradeoffs.assessment: Extension-ID allowlisting and OS-owned IPC remove the browser-accessible bridge port; the native host becomes privileged.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model the native protocol and test unauthorized extension, user, and process access.

tradeoffs.assessment: Native process and IPC add hops whose cost is unmeasured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure startup p95 and end-to-end invocation latency against loopback.

tradeoffs.assessment: A native host process may add resident memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure idle and peak RSS during five-lesson runs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Channel ownership improves, while installer, host crash, and update states add failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test host crash/restart, lost replies, upgrade, rollback, and uninstall.

tradeoffs.assessment: Signing, installers, stores, updates, support, and incidents become owned operations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run release and revocation tabletop exercises on every supported platform.

tradeoffs.assessment: The browser and local-agent adapters must migrate in parallel across platforms.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Maintain protocol parity tests and a reversible preview adapter until native acceptance passes.

residualRisks: The native host is a new privileged attack surface.
OS and browser-profile compromise remains outside the assurance claim.

acceptanceCriteria: Five lessons and revocation pass on supported platforms.
migrationNotes: Keep the preview adapter only until parity and rollback are proven.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable native distribution, unregister the host, revoke sessions, and restore the last reviewed preview adapter.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the reproducible preview under current constraints; require the signed native-host option before an ordinary-user release.

opportunities.title: Make publication a distinct reviewed state
opportunities.summary: Keep local evidence enabled while the implemented invited relay, quarantine, human review, and minimized feed remain disabled behind separate authorities.
opportunities.diagnosis: The source now implements the narrow data path and durable role-separated service controls, but no production identities, owners, key custody, privacy approval, backup policy, incident rehearsal, or approved public intake deployment exists.

evidence.claim: The draft schema is closed, enumerated, free-text-free, and origin-minimized.
Only published public-web records project, and named hosts require explicit consent plus reproduction-grade evidence.
The connector binds one public origin to a scriptless four-field preview and permits one no-retry server-to-server send only when invited relay authority is explicitly configured.
The disabled-first service enforces strict intake, quarantine, role-separated review and publication, retention, correction, and minimized signed-feed boundaries.
The source-ready loopback reviewer keeps its bearer server-side, hides private identifiers behind one-use local tokens, revalidates ledgers, and cannot publish or retry automatically.
Connecting a public endpoint before operations and privacy controls would collapse untrusted intake into an unsupported publication claim.

desiredInvariants: Every accepted public-web report starts quarantined.
Only authenticated authorized humans can advance moderation state.
Accepted-private and published are separate decisions.
Synthetic, local, raw, identifying, and instruction-shaped data never enter the feed.

options.title: Local-only evidence
options.summary: Retain the private receipt, redacted preview, and one-use local save while every external relay and service gate stays disabled.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The strict draft remains the only saved data shape.
Default configuration exposes no external send action or credential.
No external privacy or publication boundary is created.

tradeoffs.assessment: No external attack or publication surface is enabled.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify the relay and service remain disabled and synthetic/local feed eligibility remains zero.

tradeoffs.assessment: All work remains local and bounded.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure local preview and save latency only for regressions.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing bounded in-memory list is retained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify scope/item caps and release on revoke/stop.

tradeoffs.assessment: Offline operation is preserved; review data is intentionally ephemeral.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Restart the connector and confirm no durable-report claim is shown.

tradeoffs.assessment: No external service or review queue is enabled or owned.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review user copy for a clear local-only boundary.

tradeoffs.assessment: No data migration is needed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Keep service schemas separately versioned.

residualRisks: Users cannot alert a reviewer or contribute a tooling signal.
Local review state disappears by design.

workPackages: Keep local-only copy and exclusions testable.
acceptanceCriteria: No external relay or service gate is configured or enabled.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert local UI changes; no external data requires migration.

options.title: Quarantined reviewed service
options.summary: Approve and operate the implemented authenticated intake, durable moderation events, abuse/retention controls, separate publication, and minimized feed serving.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The strict draft becomes the only accepted public input.
Publication projection remains a separate gated step.
The local composer exposes only an exact four-field envelope and keeps the invited credential server-side.
The service source separates intake, moderation, publication, correction, lifecycle, and feed authority.
The reviewer workbench turns closed API transitions into explicit one-use human actions without placing the reviewer credential in browser state.
Compliance depends on operational privacy, authentication, retention, abuse, and incident controls not yet selected.

tradeoffs.assessment: Quarantine and separate publication narrow data flow, but Internet, identity, and durable-data attack surfaces are added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete authorization, abuse, privacy, injection, CSRF, SSRF, and incident reviews before external access.

tradeoffs.assessment: Validation, durable writes, moderation queries, and projection add latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure intake and feed p95/p99 under expected burst and sustained load.

tradeoffs.assessment: Indexes, queues, rate-limit state, and caches add resources.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure working set and storage growth under the retention plan.

tradeoffs.assessment: Durability improves, while retries, backpressure, outages, and correction workflows become required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject duplicate delivery, store outage, reviewer conflict, and feed rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: Human review, abuse, privacy, retention, incident, and feed operations become continuous responsibilities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Name owners and run publication/correction incident table-tops.

tradeoffs.assessment: New versioned persistence and disabled-first rollout are required; local synthetic state must remain separate.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test schema upgrades, rollback, and proof that old records cannot become published implicitly.

residualRisks: Authorized reviewers can make erroneous publication decisions.
Durable quarantine creates breach, retention, deletion, and legal obligations.
Hostname publication can cause reputational harm even after consent and review.

workPackages: Approve privacy, retention, abuse, correction, and incident policy.
Provision production identity, durable store, key custody, and backup ownership.
Complete real keyboard, screen-reader, and first-time operator acceptance for the source-ready reviewer surface.
Rehearse submission, review, publication, correction, deletion, restore, and rollback.
Enable only a tiny isolated invited cohort after approval.
acceptanceCriteria: Only authenticated human actions advance state.
Only separately published projections reach the feed.
migrationNotes: Keep local synthetic workbench and production data stores physically and logically separate.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable intake first, preserve quarantine under retention policy, and leave prior published feed versions immutable.

opportunities.recommendation: Keep the implemented relay and service disabled until named owners approve and rehearse privacy, identity, retention, abuse, backup, incident, correction, and publication operations.

openQuestions: Will Local Guard remain a developer preview or become an ordinary-user product?
Who owns extension/native-host signing, updates, revocation, and incidents?
Which identity, retention, deletion, abuse, correction, and feed policies govern reporting?
What performance, memory, availability, and review-throughput budgets apply?
